scientific_interpretation: For these two pre-registered LOW-risk clean controls, Reviewer 1 was correct without independent review and Reviewer 2 added no true material finding. The conditional policy therefore preserved protected correctness while avoiding two unnecessary reviewer calls and substantial token/latency overhead. This supports the product behavior that simple low-risk, read-only, complete-evidence prompts need not automatically invoke another LLM.
limitations: Only two clean low-risk controls were evaluated; this is not enough to set a production no-review threshold.
The pilot does not yet include low-risk cases where R1 is wrong, which are required to estimate the false-negative risk of direct finalization.
Latency values are provider/path specific and should not be generalized beyond the frozen routes used here.
Zero reported monetary cost reflects the frozen provider routes used in this pilot and is not a general cost claim.
next_required_falsification: Add LOW-risk R1-wrong controls to test whether semantic/counterfactual signals can trigger R2 without turning all low-risk work into always-review.
Add clean controls where R2 generates a false positive to measure harmful review overhead.
Compare conditional, R1-only and always-R2 across a larger mixed low/medium/high risk case set.
